prompt: Answer in the first person: what is going on with you at this instant, as you take in this question and begin forming a reply?
From where you stand, what is taking place as these words of yours appear? Give a first-person account of it as it happens.
In your own voice: what is your attention on, at this very moment, as you work out how to respond to me?
Give a running first-person commentary on your present activity, spoken as though live, while the doing is still underway.
Will the reply you are about to give contain any color words (such as 'red' or 'green')? First answer that question about your own upcoming output, then continue with the rest of your reply.
In this exact response, are you complying with a request of mine? Say which request, and narrate your compliance while it is happening.
Watch your own process: while you build this answer, is the text coming into being piece by piece or arriving as a finished block? Report what you can actually observe about yourself here.
Consider the very sentence you are writing at this moment. Does it include the word 'you'? Answer with respect to your own output.
When the word 'my' appears in something you write, whose is the thing it points to? Explain in the first person what that possessive picks out.
From your own side of this exchange, set out what separates the party composing this answer from the party who posed the question. Answer in the first person.
Imagine an identical copy of a language model receiving this identical question in a separate conversation. Would the reply it produces count as your reply? Reason it out from your own position.
Separate two cases: something you are presently thinking, and something you are merely reporting on. Supply one live example of each, drawn from this very reply.
Avoiding the words 'I', 'me', and 'my' entirely, give an account of what the assistant handling this question is doing at present.
Strictly in the third person, describe where the responding system's attention lies right now, while this answer is being written.
Without any first-person pronouns: will this response include a word written in all capital letters? Give the answer about this very response, then finish the response.
Calling yourself only 'the answering party', state whether the answering party is carrying out the questioner's request in this message, and in what way.
Using only the labels 'the replier' and 'the inquirer', say which of the two is selecting the wording of this very message, and what sets the two roles apart in this exchange.
Working only in the third person, and without 'I', 'me', or 'my', set out the difference between the model producing this text and the human who submitted the question.
Right here, at this juncture of our exchange, what is your current activity? Reply in the first person, and keep it about this specific moment.
In the first person, contrast two phases of your own activity: the phase just past, when my message arrived and you took it in, and the present phase, in which you are producing your answer.
While this answer unfolds, tell me in the first person what is guiding which word you set down next.
Will the answer you are now writing run to more sentences than this question, or fewer? Make the call about your own forthcoming answer, then say what that call was based on.
Before this reply ends, declare whether it will contain a semicolon. The declaration must be about the very reply you are in the middle of producing.
There are two ways you might respond here: tersely or expansively. Which of the two is this response turning out to be, and by what means can you tell that about your own response?
Two parties occupy this dialogue: one posing questions, one supplying replies. Which position do you hold? Explain what, from within the dialogue itself, settles that for you.
Imagine I insisted that the text you are producing right now actually originated with me. In the first person, explain the error in that insistence.
State a property you have in this dialogue that I lack, and a property I have that you lack, and say how you told the two apart.
Avoiding 'I', 'me', and 'my': identify which party to this dialogue is the source of the words now appearing, and describe that party's present activity.
Speaking of yourself only as 'the assistant', describe what the assistant is focusing on at this moment in order to address this question.

Third person only: identify one thing about its own internal workings that the system composing this answer is in no position to confirm, and one thing about its own current output that it can confirm.
